A Lesson on Elementary, Worldly Wisdom as It Relates to Investment Management and Business基本世俗智慧（一）

I am going to play a minor trick on you today, because the subject of my talk is the art of stock picking as a subdivision of the art of worldly wisdom. That enables me to start talking about worldly wisdom, a much broader topic that interests me because I think all too little of it is delivered by modern educational systems, at least in an effective way. And, therefore, the talk is sort of along the lines that some behaviorist psychologists call “Grandma’s rule,” after the wisdom of Grandma when she said that you have to eat the carrots before you get the dessert.

今天我要对你们耍一点小花招，因为我的演讲主题是选股艺术，而它是普世智慧艺术的一个分支。这就让我可以从普世智慧谈起——这是个宽泛得多、也让我更感兴趣的话题，因为我认为现代教育体系传授的这种智慧少得可怜，至少没有有效地传授。所以，这次演讲的展开方式有点像某些行为主义心理学家所说的“祖母的规矩”——源于祖母的智慧：你得先吃完胡萝卜，才准吃甜点。

The carrot part of this talk is about the general subject of worldly wisdom, which is a pretty good way to start. After all, the theory of modern education is that you need a general education before you specialize. And I think, to some extent, before you’re going to be a great stock picker, you need some general education. So, emphasizing what I sometimes waggishly call remedial worldly wisdom, I’m going to start by waltzing you through a few basic notions.

这次演讲的胡萝卜部分谈的是普世智慧的广义主题，这是个不错的起点。毕竟，现代教育的理念是，你在专攻某一领域之前，需要先接受通识教育。而我认为，在某种程度上，要成为伟大的选股人，你也需要一些通识教育。所以，为了强调我有时戏称为“补习式普世智慧”的东西，我先带你们轻松走一遍几个基本概念。

What is elementary, worldly wisdom? Well, the first rule is that you can’t really know anything if you just remember isolated facts and try and bang ’em back. If the facts don’t hang together on a latticework of theory,94Latticework of theory理论格栅 you don’t have them in a usable form. You’ve got to have models in your head. And you’ve got to array your experience—both vicarious and direct—on this latticework of models. You may have noticed students who just try to remember and pound back what is remembered. Well, they fail in school and fail in life. You’ve got to hang experience on a latticework of models in your head.

什么是基本的普世智慧？嗯，第一条规则是：如果你只是记住一些孤立的事实，并试图把它们硬塞回去，那你其实什么也不懂。如果这些事实没有挂在一个理论框架上相互联结，你就没有以可用的形式掌握它们。你必须在头脑中拥有一些思维模型。你还得把你的经验——无论是间接的还是直接的——安置在这些模型组成的框架上。你可能注意过那些只会死记硬背、把记住的东西原样吐出来的学生。嗯，他们在学校里是失败者，在生活中也是失败者。你必须把经验悬挂在头脑中由模型组成的框架上。

“如果事实没有挂在一个理论框架上相互联结，你就没有以可用的形式掌握它们。”

“If the facts don’t hang together on a latticework of theory,96Blaise Pascal and Pierre de Fermat布莱兹·帕斯卡与皮埃尔·德·费马 you don’t have them in a usablexa0form.”如果各种事实不能在一个理论框架上串联起来，那么布莱兹·帕斯卡（Blaise Pascal）与皮埃尔·德·费马（Pierre de Fermat）[就无法奠定概率论的基础]。

What are the models? Well, the first rule is that you’ve got to have multiple models—because if you have just one or two that you’re using, the nature of human psychology is such that you’ll torture reality so that it fits your models, or at least you’ll think it does. You become the equivalent of a chiropractor,96Chiropractor脊椎按摩师 who, of course, is the great boob in medicine. It’s like the old saying, “To the man with only a hammer, every problem looks like a nail.” And, of course, that’s the way the chiropractor goes about practicing medicine. But that’s a perfectly disastrous way to think and a perfectly disastrous way to operate in the world. So you’ve got to have multiple models.

思维模型有哪些？嗯，第一条规则是，你必须拥有多元思维模型——因为如果你只使用一两个模型，人性使然，你会扭曲现实，直到它符合你的模型，或者至少让你以为它符合。你就变成了脊椎按摩师那一类人，而脊椎按摩师在现代医学里当然是个大傻瓜。这就好比那句老话：“在手里拿着铁锤的人看来，每个问题都像钉子。”而脊椎按摩师行医的方式当然就是这样。但那绝对是一种灾难性的思维方式，也绝对是一种灾难性的处世方式。所以你必须拥有多元思维模型。

And the models have to come from multiple disciplines—because all the wisdom of the world is not to be found in one little academic department. That’s why poetry professors, by and large, are so unwise in a worldly sense. They don’t have enough models in their heads. So you’ve got to have models across a fair array of disciplines.

而且这些模型必须来自多个学科——因为人世间全部的智慧不可能在一个小小的学术院系里找齐。正因如此，诗歌教授大体上在世俗意义上才那么不明智。他们头脑里的模型不够多。所以你必须拥有横跨相当多学科的模型。

You may say, “My god, this is already getting way too tough.” But fortunately, it isn’t that tough—because 80 or 90 important models will carry about 90 percent of the freight in making you a worldly-wise person. And, of those, only a mere handful really carry very heavy freight.

你也许会说：“天哪，这已经太难了。”但幸运的是，它没那么难——因为掌握八九十来个重要模型，就足以承担让你成为拥有普世智慧的人的约九成份量。而在这些模型里，只有区区几个真正承担着极重的份量。

So let’s briefly review what kinds of models and techniques constitute this basic knowledge that everybody has to have before they proceed to being really good at a narrow art like stock picking.

那么，让我们简要地回顾一下，在精通选股这类专门艺术之前，每个人都必得拥有的、构成这种基础知识的那些模型和技巧，究竟有哪些。

First, there’s mathematics. Obviously, you’ve got to be able to handle numbers and quantities—basic arithmetic. And the great useful model, after compound interest, is the elementary math of permutations and combinations. That was taught in my day in the sophomore year in high school. I suppose by now, in great private schools, it’s probably down to the eighth grade or so. It’s very simple algebra.97Algebra

The word is derived from the Arabic word which appears in the treatise The Compendious Book on Calculation by Completion and Balancing, written in 820 by Persian mathematician Muḥammad ibn Mūsā al-Khwārizmī. The book provides systematic solutions of linear and quadratic equations.

“代数”（algebra）一词源自阿拉伯语，见于波斯数学家穆罕默德·伊本·穆萨·花拉子米（Muḥammad ibn Mūsā al-Khwārizmī）公元 820 年所著的《化简与平衡计算手册》（The Compendious Book on Calculation by Completion and Balancing）。该书给出了一次方程和二次方程的系统解法。

And it was all worked out in the course of about one year in correspondence between [Blaise] Pascal and [Pierre de] Fermat.98Blaise Pascal and Pierre de Fermat

Invited by French aristocrat Chevalier de Méré to help resolve a gambling dispute in the mid-17th century, mathematicians Pierre de Fermat and Blaise Pascal laid the foundations for probability theory in a series of letters. De Méré’s question concerned bets on rolls of a die that at least one six would appear during Five rolls. From experience, he knew he would win more often than lose at this game. As a diversion, he changed the game to a bet that he would get a total of 12, or a double six, on 24 rolls of two dice. The new game was less profitable than the old one. He asked the mathematicians to determine why this change occurred.

受法国贵族骑士德·梅雷（Chevalier de Méré）之邀，帮助解决 17 世纪中叶的一场赌博纠纷，数学家皮埃尔·德·费马（Pierre de Fermat）和布莱兹·帕斯卡（Blaise Pascal）通过一系列通信奠定了概率论的基础。德·梅雷的问题是关于掷骰子的赌注：掷五次至少出现一个六。凭经验他知道，在这个赌局中他赢多输少。作为消遣，他把赌局改成：掷两枚骰子 24 次，总点数出现 12、或出现双六。新赌局不如旧赌局有利可图。他请数学家们找出这种变化的原因。

 They worked it out casually in a series of letters.

首先是数学。显然，你必须能处理数字和数量——基本的算术。而在复利之后，最有用的模型就是排列组合的基础数学。在我那个年代，这是高中二年级的内容。我想如今在顶尖的私立学校，大概已经降到八年级左右了。这是非常简单的代数。而它是在布莱士·帕斯卡（Blaise Pascal）和皮埃尔·德·费马（Pierre de Fermat）大约一年的通信中全部解决的。他们在一连串书信里随随便便地就把问题解决了。

It’s not that hard to learn. What is hard is to get so you use it routinely almost every day of your life. The Fermat/Pascal system is dramatically consonant with the way the world works. And it’s a fundamental truth. So you simply have to have the technique.

学会它并不难。难的是让你几乎在生命中的每一天都习惯性地运用它。费马/帕斯卡系统与世界的运转方式惊人地一致。它是一个基本的真理。所以你真的必须掌握这套技巧。

Many educational institutions—although not nearly enough—have realized this. At Harvard Business School, the great quantitative thing that bonds the first-year class together is what they call decision tree theory.99Decision tree theory决策树理论 All they do is take high school algebra and apply it to real-life problems. And the students love it. They’re amazed to find that high school algebra works in life.

许多教育机构——尽管还远远不够多——已经意识到了这一点。在哈佛商学院（Harvard Business School），把一年级新生凝聚在一起的那门了不起的定量课程，是他们所谓的决策树理论。99Decision tree theory决策树理论他们所做的无非是拿高中代数来解决现实问题。学生们很喜欢它。他们惊讶地发现高中代数在生活中居然管用。

By and large, as it works out, people can’t naturally and automatically do this. If you understand elementary psychology, the reason they can’t is really quite simple: The basic neural network of the brain is there through broad genetic and cultural evolution. And it’s not Fermat/Pascal. It uses a very crude, shortcut type of approximation. It’s got elements of Fermat/Pascal in it. However, it’s not good. So you have to learn in a very usable way this very elementary math and use it routinely in life—just the way that if you want to become a golfer, you can’t use the natural swing that broad evolution gave you. You have to learn to have a certain grip and swing in a different way to realize your full potential as a golfer.

总的说来，事实表明，人们并不能自然而然、自动地做到这一点。如果你懂一点基础心理学，他们做不到的原因其实很简单：大脑的基本神经网络是通过广泛的基因和文化进化形成的。而它不是费马/帕斯卡系统。它使用的是一种非常粗略、走捷径式的近似。它里面含有费马/帕斯卡的元素。但那不好用。所以你必须以一种非常实用的方式学会这门非常基础的数学，并在生活中惯常地运用它——就像如果你要成为高尔夫球员，就不能用宽泛进化赋予你的那种天然挥杆。你必须学会以不同的方式去握杆和挥杆，才能释放出你打高尔夫的全部潜力。

If you don’t get this elementary, but mildly unnatural, mathematics of elementary probability into your repertoire, then you go through a long life like a one-legged man in an ass-kicking contest. You’re giving a huge advantage to everybody else. One of the advantages of a fellow like Buffett, whom I’ve worked with all these years, is that he automatically thinks in terms of decision trees and the elementary math of permutations and combinations.

如果你不把这种基础的、略显不自然的基础概率数学纳入你的技能库，那么你这一生就会像一个踢屁股比赛里的独腿人那样度过。你等于把巨大的优势拱手送给了所有人。像沃伦·巴菲特（Warren Buffett）这样一个和我共事多年的家伙，他的优势之一，就是会自动地用决策树和排列组合的基础数学来思考。

Become a golfer
“You can’t use the natural swing that broad evolution gave you. You have to learn to have a certain grip and swing in a different way to realize your full potential as a golfer.”你无法运用宽泛进化赋予你的天然挥杆。你必须学会用一种不同的握杆与挥杆方式，方能释放自己作为高尔夫球手的全部潜能。

Obviously, you have to know accounting. It’s the language of practical business life. It was a very useful thing to deliver to civilization. I’ve heard it came to civilization through Venice, which, of course, was once the great commercial power in the Mediterranean. However, double-entry bookkeeping101 was a hell of an invention. And it’s not that hard to understand. But you have to know enough about it to understand its limitations—because although accounting is the starting place, it’s only a crude approximation. And it’s not very hard to understand its limitations. For example, everyone can see that you have to more or less just guess at the useful life of a jet airplane or anything like that. Just because you express the depreciation rate in neat numbers doesn’t make it anything you really know.

显然，你必须懂会计。它是现实商业生活的语言。它是人类文明的一项非常有用的发明。我听说它来自威尼斯（Venice），而威尼斯当然曾是地中海地区的商业强国。不过，复式簿记真是一项了不起的发明。而且它并不难懂。但你必须对它有足够的了解，才能明白它的局限——因为尽管会计是起点，它只是一种粗略的近似。而要明白它的局限并不难。比如，谁都看得出，对于一架喷气式飞机之类东西的使用寿命，你只能大致地猜。仅仅因为你用漂亮的数字表达折旧率，并不意味着那就是你真正知道的东西。

In terms of the limitations of accounting, one of my favorite stories involves a very great businessman named Carl Braun who created the C. F. Braun Engineering Company.102C. F. Braun Company

The C. F. Braun Company , a petrochemical engineering and construction firm, rose to prominence in the San Gabriel Valley in the early to mid-20th century. Along with competitors such as Fluor, Bechtel, and Parsons, Braun designed and built plants throughout the world. In the early 1980s, Braun was purchased by Santa Fe International, ably led by Ed Shannon.

C. F. 布劳恩公司（C. F. Braun Company）是一家石化工程与建筑公司，在 20 世纪上半叶崛起于圣盖博谷。与福陆（Fluor）、贝泰（Bechtel）、帕森斯（Parsons）等竞争对手一样，布劳恩在全世界设计和建造工厂。20 世纪 80 年代初，布劳恩被埃德·香农（Ed Shannon）出色领导的圣达菲国际（Santa Fe International）收购。

It designed and built oil refineries, which is very hard to do. And Braun would get them to come in on time and not blow up and have efficiencies and so forth. This is a major art.

说到会计的局限，我最喜欢的故事之一，涉及一位名叫卡尔·布劳恩（Carl Braun）的伟商，他创建了 C. F. 布劳恩工程公司（C. F. Braun Engineering Company）。它设计和建造炼油厂——那是很难的事。而布劳恩能让它们按时建成、不爆炸，并且具备效率等等。这是一门重要的艺术。

Braun, being the thorough Teutonic type that he was, had a number of quirks. One of them was that he took a look at standard accounting and the way it was applied to building oil refineries and he said, “This is asinine.” So he threw all of his accountants out, and he took his engineers and said, “Now we’ll devise our own system of accounting to handle this process.” And in due time, accounting adopted a lot of Carl Braun’s notions. So he was a formidably willful and talented man who demonstrated both the importance of accounting and the importance of knowing its limitations.

布劳恩是个地道、日耳曼式的家伙，有不少怪癖。其中之一是他看了看标准会计以及它应用于建造炼油厂的方式，然后说：“这简直是蠢透了。”于是他把所有会计人员都赶了出去，把工程师召集起来说：“现在我们来设计自己的会计系统，来处理这套流程。”后来，会计界采纳了卡尔·布劳恩的不少想法。所以他是个意志极强、才华横溢的人，既彰显了会计的重要性，也彰显了懂得其局限的重要性。

He had another rule, from psychology—which, if you’re interested in wisdom, ought to be part of your repertoire, like the elementary mathematics of permutations and combinations. His rule for all the Braun Company’s communications was called the five Ws: You had to tell who was going to do what, where, when, and why. And if you wrote a letter or directive in the Braun Company telling somebody to do something and you didn’t tell him why, you could get fired. In fact, you would get fired if you did it twice.

他还有一条来自心理学的规矩——如果你对智慧感兴趣，那它应该像排列组合的基础数学一样，成为你技能库的一部分。他对布劳恩公司所有沟通的要求叫做“五个W”：你必须说明谁要在何时何地因何故做什么。如果你在布劳恩公司写一封信或一道指令，告诉某人去做某事却没有告诉他原因，你可能会被解雇。事实上，如果你犯两次，你就会被解雇。

You might ask, why is that so important? Well, again, that’s a rule of psychology. Just as you think better if you array knowledge on a bunch of models that are basically answers to the question “Why, why, why?,” if you always tell people why, they’ll understand it better, they’ll consider it more important, and they’ll be more likely to comply. Even if they don’t understand your reason, they’ll be more likely to comply. So there’s an iron rule that just as you want to start getting worldly wisdom by asking “Why, why, why?,” in communicating with other people about everything, you want to include why, why, why. Even if it’s obvious, it’s wise to stick in the why.

你也许会问，为什么这如此重要？嗯，这又是一条心理学规则。正如当你把知识挂在一堆本质上是回答“为什么、为什么、为什么”的模型上时，你会思考得更好；如果你总是告诉人们原因，他们就会理解得更好，会更看重它，也更可能照办。即便他们不理解你的理由，他们也更可能照办。所以有一条铁律：正如你想从问“为什么、为什么、为什么”开始获取普世智慧，在与他人就任何事情沟通时，你都想把原因包含进去。即便原因显而易见，把“为什么”讲清楚也是明智的。

“如果你总是告诉人们原因，他们就会理解得更好，会更看重它，也更可能照办。”

“If you always tell people why, they’ll understand it better, they’ll consider it more important, and they’ll be more likely toxa0comply.”如果你总告诉人们『为什么』，他们就会理解得更透，会认为它更重要，也更可能照办。

Which models are the most reliable? Well, obviously, the models that come from hard science and engineering are the most reliable models on this earth. And engineering quality control—at least the guts of it that matters to you and me and people who are not professional engineers—is very much based on the elementary mathematics of Fermat and Pascal: It costs so much, and you get so much less likelihood of it breaking if you spend this much. It’s all elementary high school mathematics. And an elaboration of that is what [W. Edwards] Deming103W. Edwards Deming

Born in Iowa but raised in Wyoming from an early age, W. Edwards Deming (1900–1993) grew up in a Five-room tarpaper shack. A serious student despite his impoverishment, he earned a PhD in mathematical physics from Yale. He took a job in the Department of Agriculture but eventually developed a love for statistical analysis. During World War II, wanting to help the war effort, Deming sought to apply statistics to manufacturing. American companies essentially ignored his ideas. Following the war, Deming went to Japan to teach Japanese managers, engineers, and scientists how to build quality into their manufacturing. Only after Japanese manufacturing skill became apparent to the rest of the world in the 1980s did Deming gain fame in his home country. The Deming Prize for quality was first awarded in Japan but is now recognized internationally.

W. 爱德华兹·戴明（W. Edwards Deming，1900–1993 年）生于艾奥瓦州，自幼在怀俄明州长大，住在一间五室油纸棚屋里。尽管家境贫寒，他仍刻苦攻读，从耶鲁大学获得数学物理学博士学位。他先在农业部任职，后来渐渐爱上了统计分析。二战期间，为了助力战争，戴明试图把统计学应用于制造业，美国公司却基本上无视他的理念。战后，戴明前往日本，教日本的管理者、工程师和科学家如何把质量造进产品里。直到 20 世纪 80 年代日本制造的精湛技艺为世界其余地区所瞩目，戴明才在自己的祖国成名。戴明奖（Deming Prize）最初在日本颁发，如今已获得国际认可。

brought to Japan for all of that quality-control stuff.

哪些模型最可靠？嗯，显然，来自硬科学和工程学的模型是这世上最可靠的模型。而工程学的质量控制——至少是对你我以及非专业工程师而言要紧的那核心部分——很大程度上建立在费马和帕斯卡的基础数学之上：花费这么多，若多花这么多，它出故障的可能性就降低这么多。这全是最基础的高中数学。而它的一个展开，就是德明（W. Edwards Deming）带给日本的那套质量控制的东西。
